Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors: Right knee pain with clicking after increased workouts; pain begins after ~20 minutes of running (around mile 2–3); pain worsens with knee flexion/extension during activity; transient swelling after first run that resolved with ice; knee not swollen at present; full range of motion preserved; prior ice hockey injury with a bruise several months ago; currently training for a marathon; no systemic symptoms reported.  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes): Not recorded.  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines: Ibuprofen – dose not clearly documented for this visit; 400 mg max noted by patient; Aleve (naproxen) – dose/route/frequency not documented; Melatonin – dose/route/frequency not documented; Vitamin D – dose/route/frequency not documented; Xanax – dose/route/frequency not documented; Cannabis (smoked) – dose/route/frequency not documented. Doctor topharmacist: stronger NSAID prescribed; dose/route/frequency not documented.  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus): Not recorded.  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks: Not recorded.  
- Lifestyle: Physical activity includes marathon training; recent increase in long runs; intermittent use of ibuprofen/naproxen and Aleve for joint discomfort; uses ice therapy for knee injuries; cannabis use; occasional sleep aids (melatonin; Xanax PRN). Diet not described. Tobacco use not described.  
- Hearing and vision concerns: Not recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working diagnosis: Primary consideration for right knee pain with mechanical symptoms after increased running includes meniscal tear and patellofemoral pain syndrome (PFPS). Additional, less certain possibilities include early osteoarthritis of the knee.  
- Supporting differential diagnoses from the DDx (consistent with transcript):  
  - Meniscal tear (traumatic or degenerative) – High likelihood: clicking with knee movement, pain during running, prior knee trauma, transient swelling after initial run, full ROM preserved.  
  - Patellofemoral pain syndrome / chondromalacia patellae – High likelihood: pain with knee bending and loading during running, mid-knee pain, crepitus.  
  - Osteoarthritis of the knee – Medium likelihood: activity-related mechanical pain in a middle-aged adult with intermittent prior swelling.  
- Considerations (plausible but less certain): Iliotibial band syndrome; degenerative cartilage defects; traumatic ligament injuries (e.g., ACL/MCL) though current exam notes do not demonstrate instability or locking; autoimmune inflammatory arthritis as a remote consideration; other vascular or compartment syndromes less likely given presentation.  
- Conflicts: Not recorded (no conflict between transcript and DDx).  

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification: Continue ice therapy; modulate running program to reduce pain; seek gradual return-to-running plan with rehabilitation; consider physiotherapy assessment prior to imaging.  
- Patient health goals and priorities: Achieve pain-free running with a safe rehabilitation plan; obtain professional knee assessment to guide management.  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA): Not recorded.  
- Referrals: Referral to physiotherapist for comprehensive knee assessment and rehabilitation; referral for imaging considered if persistent swelling, heat, redness, fever, knee locking, or inability to bend/stretch develops. Potential imaging (MRI) if indicated after physio assessment.  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled: Not recorded; advised to contact clinic urgently if red flags (swelling, heat, redness, fever, knee completely locking) arise.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Meniscal tear (traumatic or degenerative)  
  - Likelihood: High  
  - Justification: Clicking with knee flexion/extension, activity-related pain starting after ~2–3 miles, prior knee trauma, transient swelling after first run, ROM preserved.  
- Patellofemoral pain syndrome / chondromalacia patellae  
  - Likelihood: High  
  - Justification: Pain with bending/loading during running, mid-knee pain, crepitus, activity-related symptoms without systemic illness.  
- Osteoarthritis of the knee (degenerative)  
  - Likelihood: Medium  
  - Justification: Age in middle adulthood with overuse activity and mechanical knee symptoms; intermittent historical swelling and crepitus.  

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note)

- Missing but clinically expected elements: Vitals not recorded; BMI not recorded; immunisation status not recorded; chronic disease screening not recorded.  
- Internal conflicts or contradictions between transcript and DDx: None identified.  
- Transcript quality notes: No major issues documented; clinical decision-making based on activity-related knee pain with mechanical symptoms described by patient.
